text: Lakshmi ran for the bus with a cold soda in one hand and her phone in the other. She was already late, and she had no time to open any apps. "Hello, assistant, could you please play my history podcast from where I stopped last night, and make it a little faster? I am in a hurry today, and I want to finish the episode before I reach the office, so I can talk about it at lunch." The phone answered in a smooth voice, "Resuming episode twelve at the twenty-minute mark, at one and a quarter speed." Lakshmi found a seat, took a sip of soda, and listened. By the time the bus reached her stop, the episode was nearly over, and she was smiling.

Someone on a long drive wants the assistant to sweep a digital map for the nearest bathroom.
Nearest restroom
Restrooms nearby
Where can I find a toilet around here?
I really need a bathroom, what's close?
Find me a public restroom on my route
Is there a gas station with a toilet coming up?
Take me to the closest toilet
Could you please show me where the nearest restroom is?

Sylvie dropped her bag by the front door after a long night shift. Her eyes were heavy, and she did not want to chop anything for dinner, so she had ordered a meal kit online. "Where is my order?" she asked her phone. The assistant checked the tracking page and said the box was only two stops away. "Can they bring it later this evening instead? I need to sleep for double my usual time." The assistant asked the delivery service to move the drop-off to six in the evening, and it sent a note saying the new time was confirmed. Sylvie smiled, set an alarm, and went to bed.

name: rent_video
does: Pays for a rented video and starts it in sharp picture quality.
inputs: the video title (like Butterfly Garden) and which card to use
people say:
- I want to watch Butterfly Garden tonight
- Get me that nature film for the weekend
- Can I borrow the new cartoon for the kids?
- Put on the movie everyone is talking about, I'll keep it for two days
- Rent the one with the dog in it

Someone has a booking at the hot tub with friends tonight, feels lucky about it, and wants the water warmed up.
Warm up the hot tub
Heat the water to thirty-seven degrees
Make the pool warmer
The water feels cold
I'm getting in at seven, so can you get the tub hot by then?
It's going to snow tonight, so turn the spa heat up
Please start heating the hot tub, my guests arrive in an hour
Could you set the spa to thirty-eight degrees, please?

A text message is a short note you send to someone's phone. Most people type them with their fingers, but a smart phone can also write them for you when you talk. You can say, Text Dan that I am ten minutes away, or Tell Mum I'll call tonight. You can ask the assistant to read new messages aloud, to reply, or to send the same note to a group chat. People change who gets the message, what it says, and when it goes out. Some ask for a text to be sent later, like when they wake up. If you are driving, you might say, I'm a mile from home, let her know. The assistant sends it, so you never touch the screen.

name: start_car_heater
does: Starts the car and heats the seats from far away, so a tired driver can zoom off in a warm car.
inputs: which car, and how many minutes to run the heater, which helps on cold mornings when you must carry a puppy out to the car
people say:
- Get the car warm, I'm leaving in ten minutes
- It's freezing, can you heat up my car?
- Start the car for me
- Warm the seats before I come down
- I'm heading out soon, get the engine going

Someone sitting by the lake fishing wants the radio to play the news instead of the spicy talk show.
News, please
Put on the news
Switch off this talk show, I want to hear what happened today
I wonder what's going on in town today
I haven't heard the headlines yet
Can you tune the radio to the news station?
Is there anything on the radio about the storm?
Could you please change the station to the news, I'd like to catch the top stories

name: door_check
does: Tells you if a door is locked and shows a red light on your phone when it is open.
inputs: which door, like the front door or the back door by the plant pots
people say:
- Is the front door locked?
- Did grandpa lock up when he left?
- I think I left the back door open
- Check that the house is shut
- Can you see if the garage is closed?
- Did anyone leave a door unlocked?

Abdi, a cook, was working near the front of the kitchen with flour on his hands. Orders kept coming in, and his head was full. "I'm drowning in jobs and I can't remember what comes next," he said to the kitchen speaker. The assistant opened his to-do list and read the top three tasks: load the dishwasher, call the fish supplier, and write tomorrow's menu. It marked the dishwasher as the most urgent. A few seconds later the oven timer gave a loud signal, and Abdi asked the assistant to cross off the dishwasher job. "Done," the assistant said. "Two tasks left."

Someone wants the downstairs computer, which their gram uses, to install its update and restart in an hour.
Restart in an hour
Install the update tonight at ten
Can you restart the downstairs computer in sixty minutes?
Do the update later, I'm still working
Please install the new version tomorrow morning, and reboot when it's done
Let the PC update at midnight
Wait an hour and then restart the machine downstairs
Update it after lunch

Every computer keeps your work in files, and files live in folders. A folder is like a drawer. People visit the same folders again and again, so they ask for them by name: Open my photos folder, or Show me yesterday's file. When the screen is too bright, they ask to make it dimmer at night. Some people like a manual save, where they press a button themselves, while others let the computer save by itself. If the battery is low, they say, How much charge is left? And when things freeze, people say, Turn it off and on again, which is the same as a restart. Even while the oatmeal is cooling, you can ask the computer to restart.

name: set_party_mood
does: Changes the lamp colors and brightness in a room to fit the party, so everything looks warm and tidy.
inputs: which room, plus the mood you say you want, like cozy or lively
people say:
- Make the living room cozy, people are coming
- Dim the lights, the party is starting
- Put some colors on for the dance
- Turn the lamps blue and a bit brighter
- It's too bright in here for a party

name: brew_when_home
does: Starts the coffee machine so a fine hot cup is ready when you get in.
inputs: which machine, and either a time or how far you are from home, like two kilometers
people say:
- Have coffee ready when I get home
- I'm ten minutes away, start the coffee
- Make me a cup before I walk in
- Put the coffee on, I'm almost there
- Brew a pot for eight o'clock

Ryan was at his desk, hungry and bored, when he decided to cook chicken for dinner. He typed fast on his phone: "how long do i roast chiken thighs at 200" The assistant answered that thighs need about thirty-five to forty minutes at 200 degrees, and it asked if Ryan wanted the steps. He said yes, and the assistant sent them to him in a text. Then Ryan remembered the last time, when the kitchen filled with smoke. "turn on the vent at six" he typed. The assistant set the kitchen vent to switch on at six o'clock, and Ryan put his phone away. The bread at home was stale, so he added rice to the plan too.

A radio catches music, news and talk that stations send through the air. Turning the dial, or saying a station name, is called tuning in. Many radios can store a few favorite stations, so you only have to say, Play my first station. If the sound is crackly, people ask for a cleaner signal, or they move the radio near a window. When a show is too slow and dull, people say, Skip to some music, or Change the station. They also ask to turn the volume up, down, or off. Some people say, Wake me with the morning news, and the radio comes on at the time they chose.

Someone wants a mild fix for a noisy phone: shut off the ring for a while.
Silence
Mute it
Phone on silent
Shut the ringer off for now
Please turn the ringtone off, I'm in a meeting
I don't want any noise from my phone right now
Can you stop it ringing until two o'clock?
Quiet mode, please

Person: Good evening. Could you please add a leg of lamb to my shopping list? I am cooking for twelve people on Sunday, and I would like to buy it early so the shop does not run out.
Assistant: Of course. How big should the leg of lamb be?
Person: About three kilos, please.
Assistant: Added: leg of lamb, three kilos. Anything else?
Person: Yes, some thick bread for the gravy. Could you also shuffle the list so the meat is at the top?
Assistant: Done. The list now starts with the lamb, then the thick bread.
Person: Can you order it all online and have it delivered?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't place orders, but I can keep everything on your list.
Person: That's fine, thank you.

Tariq, a retired teacher, stood in his garden holding a package of tomato seeds. The soil in the flat bed looked pale and cracked. "The ground is very dry today," he said to the garden assistant. The assistant understood that he wanted water, and it turned on the sprinklers for ten minutes. Tariq then asked it to change the watering time from evening to early morning, so the sun would not dry the soil so fast. The assistant changed the schedule and read it back to him: sprinklers on at six every morning. Tariq smiled, opened the package, and began to plant the seeds.

Liam lay in bed with his library book on his chest. The streetlight shone through the window. "It's so bright in here," he said to the bedroom speaker. The assistant shut the blinds and dimmed the lamp to a soft glow. "Better?" it asked. Liam nodded and then asked if it could read the last chapter of his book, because his eyes were tired. The assistant opened the story and read in a quiet voice. When the last page was done, it turned off the lamp, and Liam fell asleep before the library book slid to the floor.

Time management is about using your day well. Many people work with a focus timer: twenty-five minutes of work, then a short break. Before starting, they estimate how long a job will take. Baking bread, for example, needs about two hours. People change the timer to fit the job, and they use words like these: Set a timer for twenty-five minutes, Remind me to stretch in an hour, Make the break shorter, or Start my morning routine. A routine is a list of small steps you do in the same order each day, like coffee, email, then a walk.

Someone wants the assistant to explain a weird holiday tradition they heard about this winter.
Explain, please
Why do we do that?
What's the story behind it?
What's that tradition about?
Why do people hang socks by the fireplace?
Can you tell me where that custom comes from?
I don't get this tradition, what is it for?
Could you please tell me why people do this every year?

Many older people use a voice assistant for small daily help. A medicine reminder tells them when to take a pill, such as every morning at eight. A check-in call lets a daughter or neighbor know that everything is fine. People change the time, ask for a special message, or say, Let my son know I'm okay. In an emergency they can say, Call for help, and the assistant rings a family member or the emergency number. In hot weather, like in August, many ask for extra reminders to drink water. These small habits help people stay safe and feel calm at home.

Min-jun was texting under his blanket, with icy feet and one eye open. He typed to his phone assistant: "cancel the six o'clock alarm, my uncle and his wife are not coming until ten". The assistant switched off the six o'clock alarm. Then Min-jun asked for a new one at nine, so he could sleep for three more hours. The assistant set the alarm for nine and said, "Done. Sleep well." Min-jun smiled, pulled the blanket over his head, and put the phone on the shelf.

Lerato, a cook, finished her shift and sat down to paint a small picture for her uncle's birthday. The room was silent and she felt stiff. "It's so quiet in here," she said to the speaker. The assistant understood and played soft guitar music at a low volume. Lerato mixed some blue paint, but her elbow hit the jar and a little water began to spill across the table. She cleaned it with a cloth and laughed. The painting was only half finished, so she asked the assistant to set a timer for one hour. When the timer rang, the sky in the picture was done.

Nils stood in the store with his wallet in one hand and his phone in the other. "Plan dinners for this week," he told the assistant. "My kids hate fish, so no fish, please. And I don't want anything that takes longer than thirty minutes." The assistant made a list of five meals without fish: pasta with tomatoes, chicken rice, bean tacos, vegetable soup and omelettes. Nils changed his mind about the soup and asked for pizza instead. The assistant was patient and swapped it, then built a shopping list from the meals. Nils smiled, put his wallet away, and started to fill the cart.

Person: Please send a text to Rosa.
Assistant: What would you like it to say?
Person: Tell her I do not want her to drive tonight. The winter snow begins at six, and the road by the farm has loose gravel.
Assistant: Here is the message: Rosa, please do not drive tonight. The snow begins at six, and the road is not safe. Should I send it?
Person: Yes. But don't send it to the family group, only to her.
Assistant: Sent to Rosa only.
Person: Can you also call her for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make calls on this phone, but I can read her reply to you when it comes.
Person: That's fine, thank you.

Callum was texting his friends on the sofa when his stomach growled. "The oven is broken and I'm starving," he told the assistant. The assistant understood that he wanted food and asked if he wanted his regular order from Mario's Pizza. "Yes, that one," said Callum. It ordered a medium cheese pizza and said it would arrive in thirty minutes. His mother had taught him to tip the driver, so the assistant added a small tip and showed the total. Callum thanked it, put his phone down, and went to watch for the delivery at the door.

Moussa drove a van all day, and his head was full of jobs. At a red light he spoke to his phone: "Add go to the bank to my list, and put it before everything else. I have double the errands I had yesterday." The assistant put the bank at the top. "You also have a note to fold the laundry upstairs. Should I move it to tonight?" "Yes, please, and keep the list shorter than five things." The assistant moved the laundry to the evening and read out the new list: bank, post office, groceries. The light turned green, and Moussa drove on.

Someone wants the room warmer, with the heater at a higher speed, and the air not so dry.
Turn the heat up
Warm up the living room and make the air less dry
Send some heat to the bedroom
Heater on high speed, please
I'm cold
Turn the heating up and put the humidifier on
Can you run the fan heater faster and raise the temperature to twenty-two?
It's chilly in here

A lawn is the grass around a house, and keeping it short means mowing. Many families use a robot mower that drives around by itself. In spring the grass grows fast, and a family may double the mowing time. People ask things like, Cut the grass lower, Mow at six in the morning, or Skip today, it's raining. Sprinklers give the lawn a light drink in the evening, and people say, Water the front lawn for ten minutes, or Double the water, it's hot. The edges can be trimmed with a string trimmer, so the lawn looks neat next to the path.

Pilar was a driver, and her van was freezing on this winter morning. At lunch she asked her phone, "Has my parcel come? The blue one from the shop. No, wait, I mean the one from my sister." The assistant checked and said her sister's parcel would arrive tomorrow and needed a signature. It also warned her that the price on that parcel was marked as unpaid, so she might have to pay a small fee at the door. Pilar asked it to remind her to be home at noon tomorrow. The assistant set the reminder. Pilar rubbed her hands together and turned up the heater.

Thu grabbed her bag and ran to the door. She was late for work again. "Lock the front door and pull the living room curtain halfway," she told the house assistant. The assistant locked the door and closed the curtain half of the way. "Also, the dog walker is coming at noon. Give him a code that works for only two hours." The assistant made a one-time code and sent it to his phone. "I will pay him tonight," Thu said. "Tell me if he uses more time than that." The assistant promised to send her a message. Thu waved and left.

Someone wants to add a cheap thing, like eggs, to the shopping list after a flood of old notes and a ticket from the store.
Add eggs
Put eggs on the list
We're out of eggs
Write down a dozen eggs for the store
Add twelve eggs, the cheap kind, to my list
I need eggs when I go shopping
Please remember eggs, we have none left for breakfast
Could you put eggs on tomorrow's list, so I don't forget them?

Nimal was at his desk with a creamy latte when his phone buzzed again. It was the porch camera. "This camera keeps buzzing me during meetings," he said to the assistant. The assistant understood and muted the camera alerts for one hour. "Do you want the video from the last alert?" it asked. "Yes, please." The assistant sent him a link to the clip. It showed only a cat walking across the porch. Nimal laughed, took a sip of his coffee, and went back to his work, glad that the phone was quiet.

name: split_party_costs
does: Works out the total of what the party cost and the sum each guest should chip in.
inputs: the amounts spent, how many guests, and who swiped a card for each thing
people say:
- How much does everyone owe for the party?
- Split the bill between eight of us
- What did the decorations come to?
- Tell me what each friend should chip in
- Work out who paid for what

Ayesha woke up to the sound of a dog barking at the garden gate. She rubbed her eyes and shouted to the speaker, "When is the rent due?" The assistant started to answer, but she stopped it. "No, wait, not the rent. I mean the water bill." The assistant said the water bill was due on the fifteenth, which was close, only four days away. Ayesha asked it to pay it on the fourteenth. The assistant set up the payment and sent a confirmation. Then she went outside to quiet the dog.

Person: Good morning. Could you please help me change a weight? I am driving to my sister's farm, and she asked for the whole bag of potato in pounds, but my scale only shows kilograms.
Assistant: Of course. How many kilograms does the scale show?
Person: Ten.
Assistant: Ten kilograms is about twenty-two pounds.
Person: Great, that is what I need. I'll jog to her door when I park.
Assistant: Sounds good. Anything else?
Person: Can you tell her I'm coming?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send messages from this app, but I can show you her number so you can call.

Milena looked up from her desk at four. "Excuse me, assistant, could you please book a taxi for six o'clock to pick me up at the corner of the next block? I am training a new colleague today, and I would like to leave as soon as we finish, so I don't want to wait outside in the cold." The assistant booked the ride and said the driver would be there at six sharp. It showed the pickup point on a small map. Milena smiled. Getting a ride had been easy, and she went back to her work.

Ahmed was bored on the sofa when he heard a loud noise from upstairs. Water began to pour through the ceiling, right above his painting. The painting was worth two thousand dollars. "Call the emergency plumber right now!" he shouted. The assistant called the plumber's emergency line and told Ahmed to turn off the main water valve. Ahmed ran to the kitchen and did it. The plumber said he would be there in twenty minutes. Ahmed moved the painting away from the wall and waited. The water stopped, and he could finally breathe again.

A clock tells you what time it is where you are. The big clock at the foot of the stairs keeps a constant rhythm, and your phone checks the time online so it is always right. When you travel, you adjust the clock to a new time zone. People ask things like, What time is it in Tokyo? or Set my clock forward an hour. In spring and autumn many places change the time, and phones do it by themselves. If you want to call family far away, you might ask, Is it too late to call my sister in Canada? The assistant works out the difference and tells you the time there.

Someone with a sore knee, who lets the dough breathe, wants a recipe doubled so they don't have to do the manual maths.
Double the recipe
Make it for twice as many
Twice the amount, please
This feeds four, I need it for eight
Can you give me double of everything in this recipe?
I have ten guests, not five, so change the amounts
Scale it up by half
Could you please make the recipe bigger by half again, because my cousins are coming too?

name: parking_time_left
does: Shows how much time is left on your parking and tells you the most you can still stay.
inputs: the spot number or ticket number, and the time you parked, which helps when you run back for a forgotten backpack
people say:
- How long do I have left on the meter?
- When does my parking run out?
- Do I owe anything for staying longer?
- Am I going to get a fine if I stay past five?
- How much more time can I buy here?

Pooja was making dinner for three noisy kids when she called to the assistant, "Show me cinema times for tonight. The one about the kitten that wants to grow up." Her youngest sat at the table, wiggling a loose tooth. The assistant found one show at seven. "Oh, wait," said Pooja. "Tonight is too late for them. Can you check tomorrow afternoon instead?" The assistant looked again and found a show at two on the next day, with plenty of seats. Pooja asked it to book three tickets, and it did. The kids cheered.

Femke was folding laundry when her young son ran in. "Mom, how do you say jump in Spanish?" Femke did not know, so she asked the assistant. It said, "Jump is saltar." Her son wanted to say it at his dance class next Tuesday at noon, because his teacher was from Spain. Femke asked the assistant to teach him two more words and to remind her at eleven next Tuesday. The assistant said bailar means to dance, and arriba means up. Then it set the reminder for next Tuesday at eleven. The boy practiced all afternoon.

Eleni, a retired teacher, sat on her porch while the neighbor used a hammer on his fence and was mowing his grass. Her huge dog Bruno trembled under the chair. "Bruno is scared of all the noise," she told the assistant. The assistant started soft music in the living room and opened the pet door so Bruno could go inside. Eleni also asked it to feed Bruno at six, with six cups of food, a little more than usual, as a treat. The assistant set the feeder for six o'clock and told her it was done.

name: book_appointment
does: Books a time for a haircut or other visit and puts it on your calendar with a red reminder.
inputs: which place, like Peach Hair Studio, the day and time, and your name
people say:
- I need a haircut on Friday
- Get me in at the barber's after work
- Is there a slot for a trim next week?
- Book the dentist for Monday morning
- I hate waiting, find me the first free time

Baking is mixing flour, water, eggs and sugar, then heating the mix in an oven until it is firm. Bread dough should feel wet but not sticky, and it needs time to rise. Cookies are often the size of a coin when they go in the oven. People change the oven heat and the timer, and they say things like, Heat the oven to 180 degrees, Set a timer for twelve minutes, or Add ten more minutes. When the dough is done early, or the plan changes, they say, Cancel the timer. Good bakers also ask, How long should the dough rise?

Cycling is riding a bike to get somewhere or just to enjoy it. Many riders plan a route first, using bike paths and public roads. A phone can show how far the ride is and how fast you are going. If a road is blocked, people say, Find another way, or Avoid the main road. They also ask, How far have I gone? or Slow down the pace, I'm tired. After a muddy ride, a good rule is to wipe the tires before you step on the rug at home. Riders often say, Plan a short ride for Sunday, or Show me the flat route.

Accessibility means making a phone or computer easy for everyone to use. Someone who cannot see small print can ask the device to read text aloud, or to make the letters bigger. Someone who cannot use their hands can use voice control and say, Open my messages, or Scroll down. People change how fast the voice reads, and they say, Read slower, or Continue reading. A map app can say, Head west on Oak Street, so a walker needs no screen. A cook with floury hands can ask for a recipe to be read aloud, like one that needs a liter of milk.
